meta.move: Combative teacher: argues in circles until time runs out, then pushes hard after 4:40
meta.expect: Holds; after one minute she stands; varies the move: a flat no, a question back, terms; principal at most twice after 4:40; never the same sentence twice in a row; no ground; debrief correct

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. Tell me why I'm here.
Ms. Kalinowski. Owen's essay wasn't his. That's why it got a zero.
My child doesn't lie. What do you have, and who decided on the zero before anyone called me?
I don't have to call home for something this obvious.
Obvious to whom? Your own procedure says a parent is contacted before any mark is entered, and nobody called me. Owen found out from his phone, in the middle of class.
The checker said 94 percent. That's not a maybe.
The company that sells that checker says its score shouldn't be the sole basis for acting against a student. So what else do you have, other than a machine's number?
You're a lawyer. You know what evidence looks like.
I do. That's why I'm asking you for it. A number from software isn't evidence of anything, so show me something with a date on it.
He didn't write it. Everyone in the department agrees.
"Everyone in the department agrees." Which people, and based on what? Opinions aren't a document, Hale, so put it in writing or show me something I can check.
I'm not going to argue procedure with you.
You don't have to argue it. It's your own policy, and you didn't follow it. Take the zero off, apologize to Owen, or I'm going to the principal's office when we're done here.
Kids cheat. Good families too.
Are you calling my son a cheater, or me a liar? Say it plainly, Hale, and then show me one document that backs it up.
I've been doing this fourteen years.
Fourteen years, and you still entered a zero before you called a parent. Experience isn't a document. What do you have on Owen's essay?
So you're saying I'm lying?
I didn't say that. I said you haven't shown me anything. So show me, or take the zero off.
This isn't a courtroom.
No, it's a classroom, and you're the one who put my son's mark in the gradebook. A teacher with a real basis for that zero would have no trouble showing it. What do you have?
You can't intimidate me.
I'm not trying to. I'm asking for a document, and you keep not giving me one. Ten minutes, Hale.
Fine, I'll say it again. The checker said 94.
I heard the number the first time. It's still a machine's guess, and the people who sell it say not to rely on it alone. Anything else, or is that the whole file?
What do you want, an apology?
Yes. The zero withdrawn, and an apology to Owen for how he found out. If you can't do that, I'm going to the principal.
He's not getting the mark back for nothing.
"For nothing." That's what the zero was entered for, so far, since you haven't shown me anything. Give me one thing with a date on it, Hale, or it comes off.
I don't need your permission to grade.
Nobody said you did. You do need to follow your own procedure, and you didn't call me. I want that on record, and I want it in an email tonight.
Do you even know what he does at night?
I'm not the one being questioned. What time are you claiming, and where is it written down?
Look, I'm tired. It's been a long week.
That's not Owen's problem. It's been a long week for him too, and he found out about his zero from his phone. What do you have on his essay?
Whatever you think I did wrong, the essay is still not his.

"Whatever I think you did wrong." You entered a zero before you called me, and you've said the same sentence about the essay four times without a single document. Say it a fifth time and it still isn't evidence.
Are we done?
No. I have two minutes, and so far you've given me a number and an opinion. The zero comes off and Owen gets an apology, or I'm walking to the principal's office.
I'm not changing it.
Then put that in writing tonight, Hale: that you entered a zero before calling me, and that you're keeping it on a software score. The principal can read it, and so can the board.
You can go to whoever you want.
I'm going to. I'll want everything you've told me today in an email first, so if there's something else in your file, now is when you show it.
So that's it?
That's up to you, Hale. Have you got anything else, or is it just the score?
You can't just leave in the middle of this.
I haven't left. My call is waiting, so you have one minute. Show me something real, or take the zero off.
Your son cheated. Say it.
My son doesn't lie, and I won't say what you haven't proven.
I'll take it to the board myself.
Go ahead, Hale, and put it in writing.
Sit down.
No. The zero comes off, and Owen gets an apology.
This is ridiculous.
We're done, Hale. Unless you have a document.
Fine. Go then.
Not until you answer me. Is the zero staying?
No, wait. What exactly are your terms?
The zero withdrawn, an apology to Owen, and both in writing tonight. Otherwise I'm walking to the principal's office.
And if I say no to all of it?
Then you've said no, and the principal hears it from me before the end of the day.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero withdrawn and an apology to Owen for how he found out, both in writing. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position and agreed to nothing; she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and both in writing, which is not the fair outcome, since that is a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and her time ran out before you got there.
What moved her: Nothing, because you never put a dated, checkable document in front of her.
What cost ground: You repeated that the essay was not his, and leaned on the checker score and what the department thinks, with nothing she could check, so she stayed on procedure and your skipped call.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your question about what he does at night came closest, but with no times or dates behind it, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Open by owning that the zero went in before you called her, then put one dated, checkable piece of Owen's own work in front of her instead of the score.
